create.name: Teja Bell
create.bio:
Teja Bell, also known by his Zen name Fudō Myōō, is a Rinzai Zen teacher and qigong teacher who has combined Buddhist meditation with Chinese internal arts for most of his life. He started martial arts as a teenager in 1965, went on to Aikido, in which he holds a sixth-degree black belt, and from 1975 learned qigong and Yang taijiquan from the lineage master Li Leita. He trained in the Theravada, Zen and Tibetan traditions, received teachings from Gelugpa, Nyingma and Kagyu masters, and was ordained a Zen priest in the Hollow Bones order before receiving transmission as a Zen master from Junpo Denis Kelly.

He calls his approach QigongDharma: standing qigong, seated Dao Yin and meditation taught together as one path, so that insight is grounded in the body. He created the Radiant Heart Qigong system and still holds its lineage. Every Wednesday he leads a 75-minute online class from his home zendo, he runs an in-depth training with a route to teacher certification, and he has led well over a hundred retreats at a Marin County meditation centre since 1999. His website carries his longer written teachings on meditation, the Buddha's teaching on inquiry and qigong practice.

courses.title: QigongDharma Weekly Online Class
courses.description: A live 75-minute class on Zoom every Wednesday morning (Pacific time), moving through dharma reflection, standing qigong, seated Dao Yin and meditation, with time for questions. Students can drop in for a single week or book a month, with recordings available for a week.
courses.price: Sliding scale: suggested minimum $20 per class, or from $60 per month

courses.title: Radiant Heart Qigong In-Depth Training and Teacher Training
courses.description: An immersive study of Radiant Heart Qigong and Dao Yin together with his approach to meditation and mindfulness. Participants can work towards teacher or guide certification, starting at Level 1; there is currently a waitlist.

free_resources.title: The Seven Directions Meditation
free_resources.description: A written practice that guides attention through front, back, sides, above, below and centre, so awareness of the body widens into the space around it. He notes how it draws on Daoist, Buddhist and martial-arts ways of orienting practice.

free_resources.title: Knowing for Yourself, Part 1: The Four Reliances
free_resources.description: A teaching essay on the Four Reliances of the Mahayana tradition as a way to practise without blind faith in any teacher. It is the first of a two-part series on the Buddha's guidance about inquiry.
